title: Emergency tenant-scope retry-dampener and cross-environment failover shim to contain cascading 5xx during partial infra partition
creator: Maya Patel
description: During a partial network partition between hosted frontends and a set of Dedicated pools we observed sustained tenant-scoped 5xx bursts. Customers reported timeouts and repeated client retries that amplified backend load, causing cascading failures and two P1 escalations. This ticket implements an emergency containment shim: a tenant-scoped retry dampener (token-bucket + exponential decay), a short-circuit path to divert afflicted tenants to a graceful degraded fastpath, and an emergency cross-environment routing override (route to customer's Dedicated/Private fallback when available). The goal is to stop amplification, buy time for infra remediation, and provide transparent customer communication with mitigations until a permanent fix is rolled out.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant retry tokens rate-limits repeated attempts within a configurable decay window (default 30s) and emits telemetry for every dampened request
Affected tenants can be programmatically placed into a degraded fastpath that returns cached/partial responses within 200-400ms tail latency
Cross-environment routing override successfully redirects compatible requests to customer Dedicated/Private endpoints with end-to-end trace propagation preserved
Runbook and oncall playbook updated and validated via a simulated tenant surge drill
No regression on normal steady-state latency for unaffected tenants (<=2% p95 change)
implementation_notes: Add a lightweight in-edge token-bucket keyed by tenant-id + route hash; bucket tokens regenerated using exponential decay to avoid fixed windows
Implement dampener as a non-blocking filter: first few retries still pass (grace tokens) but then receive 429-like dampening response with Retry-After header and structured telemetry
Fastpath: integrate existing cached prefix responder used for embeddings (read-only) to return partial or precomputed fallback payloads for common prompt templates
Cross-env routing: use smart-routing flags keyed by tenant feature-flag. If tenant has Dedicated/Private fallback registered, set a transient override route for 5 minutes with circuit metrics
Telemetry: add event types tenant.retry_dampened, tenant.fastpath_activated, tenant.crossenv_override. Ensure these are surfaced in Console and linked to an incident dashboard
Add feature flag gating, emergency kill-switch (configstore), and an automated TTL so overrides do not persist if operators forget to clear them
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (edge-only canary): deploy token-bucket dampener behind feature-flag to 5% of frontends (non-customer-facing tests)
Stage 2 (tenant pilot): enable for two impacted customers (consent requested in escalation comms), runbook owner to monitor metrics for 2 hours
Stage 3 (region ramp): with passed metrics ramp to 50% of traffic in the affected region, enable fastpath caching for common prompt templates
Stage 4 (global safe-open): if sustained improvement and no regressions, flip global feature-flag and enable cross-env routing for tenants that registered fallbacks
Rollback plan: immediate feature-flag flip to disable; observe telemetry; auto-rollback if p95 latency delta > 10% or error rate increases
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket state transitions, jittered token regeneration, and metrics emissions
Integration test: simulate N-tenants with convex retry patterns to ensure rate-limits reduce backend QPS by >60% under surge
Chaos test: introduce partial network partition between frontends and Dedicated pools in staging; validate cross-env override maintains successful request delivery for registered tenants
Load test: verify unaffected tenants see <=2% p95 latency change when dampener is active at 50% rollout
Runbook drill: oncall runs the simulated tenant surge and practices manual override and rollback steps

notes: Keep the dampener lightweight: it must not add blocking calls to the hot path; prefer in-memory sharded maps with periodic compaction
Coord with SDK team to add a soft Retry-After handler that surfaces dampening to client logs to reduce blind replays
After stabilization, evaluate permanent changes: KV lease shrink, eviction heuristics (reduce thrash), and more conservative client-side backoff guidance
Follow-up tickets to track: permanent routing policy changes, telemetry retention for tenant surge events, and SDK guidance updates
